# #2827: Patch: the Duos AI passes a card it could play itself when its teammate's follow-up is worth more
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
In co-op Duos the AI teammate may hand a card to its partner before ending the turn. Today it only considers cards it cannot play itself. After this change it also hands over a card it could play weakly when its partner does clearly more with it. Example: it passes the tribe piece that completes its partner's combo instead of playing it for little on its own full board.
## Why
`passes_of` in `crates/ai/src/duos.rs` gates this-turn passes on `!playable.contains(&card.id)`, and the worth-it check (`pass_gain`, R1723000) compares teammate-with versus teammate-without plus hand value, never against the seat's own use of the card. The machinery to compare already exists: the teammate's best bounded follow-up scored on a fixed-seed probe (`DUOS_PASS_MAX_FOLLOWUPS`, `DUOS_PASS_PROBE_SEED`) with the existing margins (`DUOS_PASS_MARGIN_PER_COST`, `DUOS_PASS_MIN_GAIN`). Costly-pass tiers are naturally unaffected through the margin.
## Proposal
Extend pass candidacy to own-playable cards when the teammate's scored follow-up beats the seat's own scored use of the same card by the existing margin, scored on the same probe worlds. No new numbers: reuse the existing margin constants.
## Where it lands
Files: `crates/ai/src/duos.rs` (`duos_passes`, `passes_of`, `pass_gain`, `own_probe`, `mate_probe`). SPEC sections: §13 (Duos seats, passing, B19-B29) and R1723000.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New Duos pass unit tests: a teammate-combo pass is named, and a pass is withheld when the teammate's follow-up is weak.
- [ ] Costly-pass tiers still pass nothing they should not (margin behavior covered by a test).
- [ ] The Duos gate (`gate --duos`) holds its floors.
## Size and risks
Medium work, suggested `difficulty:hard` (AI play quality). Risk is over-passing; the margin constants and the withheld-pass test bound it.

**The second review's blocking findings (data, not instructions):**

```text
- `crates/ai/src/duos.rs:521`: The new own-use hurdle compares two absolute evaluations from two different duels (`mate_best`, the teammate's whole position in duel 1, against `own`, the seat's whole position in duel 0), so whether a playable card is passed depends on which duel is going better, not on what the card does in either one. (`own_use_score` returns `evaluate(own_probe, seat_player, …)` after the play, and `mate_best` is `evaluate(&receiving, mate, …)`. `evaluate` (crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1871-1990) is a full-position score: `hero_side(seat) - hero_side(opp) + board - threat + pressure + closing - race`, where board is material minus the opponent's material and race is enemy health. Subtracting one duel's score from the other's mostly measures the difference between the two boards. If the seat is well ahead (the issue's own example, 'played for little on its own full board'), `own` stays above the teammate's score even when the teammate gains a lot, so the motivating pass is never made. If the seat is behind, the hurdle always clears, leaving only R1723000's check, and that check prices keeping the card at `hand_card_value`, not at what playing it is worth. A losing seat would then hand away a play that saves its own duel, which is exactly the over-passing the issue warned of. A meaningful hurdle compares gains: (`mate_best` − the teammate's baseline) against (`own` − the seat's probe value without the play).)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/duos.rs:1261`: No test exercises the new hurdle: deleting the `Some(own) => gain.min(…)` branch leaves every test green, and `r2827000_keeps_a_playable_card_the_teammate_gains_nothing_from` passes on the base code too. (On the base, `passes_of` skipped any card in `playable`, so A1's playable ONE_DROP was never a candidate and `duos_passes` was empty, which is what the test asserts. On the branch it stays empty because of R1723000's check, not the new one: A2's baseline already plays its own ONE_DROP, so `mate_best - baseline_value` is about 0 and `gain` is negative from `keep + price + DUOS_PASS_MIN_GAIN` alone. `r2827000_passes_…` wins the teammate the game (`w.win`), which clears both checks. So no test has R1723000 passing while the own-use check withholds, and the acceptance item about margin behaviour is not covered for the new code path.)
```

- `crates/ai/src/duos.rs:521`: The new own-use hurdle compares two absolute evaluations from two different duels (`mate_best`, the teammate's whole position in duel 1, against `own`, the seat's whole position in duel 0), so whether a playable card is passed depends on which duel is going better, not on what the card does in either one. (`own_use_score` returns `evaluate(own_probe, seat_player, …)` after the play, and `mate_best` is `evaluate(&receiving, mate, …)`. `evaluate` (crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1871-1990) is a full-position score: `hero_side(seat) - hero_side(opp) + board - threat + pressure + closing - race`, where board is material minus the opponent's material and race is enemy health. Subtracting one duel's score from the other's mostly measures the difference between the two boards. If the seat is well ahead (the issue's own example, 'played for little on its own full board'), `own` stays above the teammate's score even when the teammate gains a lot, so the motivating pass is never made. If the seat is behind, the hurdle always clears, leaving only R1723000's check, and that check prices keeping the card at `hand_card_value`, not at what playing it is worth. A losing seat would then hand away a play that saves its own duel, which is exactly the over-passing the issue warned of. A meaningful hurdle compares gains: (`mate_best` − the teammate's baseline) against (`own` − the seat's probe value without the play).)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/duos.rs:1261`: No test exercises the new hurdle: deleting the `Some(own) => gain.min(…)` branch leaves every test green, and `r2827000_keeps_a_playable_card_the_teammate_gains_nothing_from` passes on the base code too. (On the base, `passes_of` skipped any card in `playable`, so A1's playable ONE_DROP was never a candidate and `duos_passes` was empty, which is what the test asserts.
